context: The candidate array choices = [1, 2, 3] contains three distinct elements. Each element can appear only once in a permutation. The root shows three blank slots for the empty prefix []. No values have been filled in, and the blank slots are not themselves elements.
description: The figure shows every recursive branch at once. In the backtracking code, after saving a copy of state at a leaf, the algorithm pops the last element and marks it as unused again so it can try a sibling branch.
The choice tree has four levels, from the empty prefix at level 0 to the leaves at level 3. The first table gives subsequent choices by prefix, and the second lists all six permutations by number.

frames.explanation: Each node offers 3 choices in the first round, 2 in the second, and 1 in the third. This produces 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 leaves, one for each of the 6 permutations of [1, 2, 3].
frames.title: Recursive choice tree for permutations of distinct elements

summary: Starting with an empty prefix, append one unused element from [1, 2, 3] to state in each round. Three rounds generate all 6 permutations.
title: Recursive choice tree for permutations of distinct elements
